body:
Ruling: batch #231 item 1 · letter B · maintainer 「同意 B」 2026-09-28T02:58Z

Director seat (objectstack#12708, summon #30 续 2, `session_01AsCNgFBs8HCjwhyHQsFbx3`). Provenance: maintainer, live PM chat with the director seat, 2026-09-28, replying to batch #231 (this card, item 1, recommendation B, presented with the full four-axis body); verbatim 「同意 B」.

**Ruled: B.** The eight identity members of `api.documentation` — `title`, `description`, `termsOfService`, `contact.name` / `contact.url` / `contact.email`, `license.name` / `license.url` — are ENFORCED: an authored value overlays the served `info` on both doors (`/api/v1/openapi.json` and the environment-scoped door); nothing authored ⇒ the served `info` is byte-identical to the artifact. `documentation.version` is RETIRED: the served `info.version` stays `SPEC_VERSION`, exactly as #11646 (`5405070350`) ruled, and an authored `version` is refused at publish time by a `retiredKey()` tombstone whose message names the protocol version as the one source and points an app's own release number to `description`. A (all nine overlay, version included) and C (retire all nine) are not taken.

Readings that decided it:
- Long-term: the cover's version is a fact of the protocol, owned by `packages/spec`; the cover's name, contact, terms and licence are the publisher's identity. One truth per field. #11646's motive stands — an integrator must be able to read which protocol version they are talking to — and #18900's criterion (`5727134555`) is applied to the identity keys, where the API-management mainstream lets the owner sign the cover. A would make `info.version` a contested field again, in a third meaning; C would tell an app owner the document they publish is always signed ObjectStack.
- Mainstream (from memory, not re-read): Azure API Management, Apigee, ServiceNow Scripted REST and Power Platform custom connectors let the API owner set the whole cover; the metadata-generated peers (PostgREST under Supabase, Directus) keep the cover engine-owned, engine-versioned. The split supports neither wholesale rule; B follows the field's owner.
- Real use: zero authors of `api.documentation` in the three repos; the change is small in every direction, so cost did not decide.
- AI-safety: the current state (nine keys parsed, none honoured) is the worst one. B leaves no silent key: eight are honoured, one refuses loudly. The same block already carries a `retiredKey()` tombstone (`enabled`, #20295), so a mixed block is the repo's existing pattern, not a new one.

Execution parameters (ruled in the same stroke; no further decision card):
- #20294 is re-dispatched on the dev's kept worktree and resume plan as the seat's own B: eight keys ENFORCE + `documentation.version` RETIRE. Lane `domain:spec`, `priority:p3` unchanged; a `packages/rest` sub-issue only if triage's anchoring rule requires one. Clause-② yes (behaviour change on a public document; `title` becomes `.optional()`, `version` tombstoned) ⇒ `@objectstack/spec` `minor`, `@objectstack/rest` per its bump policy; `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.
- Semantics: `title` becomes `.optional()` (the materialized default `'ObjectStack API'` was never served; the artifact's `'ObjectStack REST API'` is the default). `contact` and `license` replace the bundled block whole, never member by member (an MIT name at the Apache URL would be a false statement in a machine-read contract). The overlay lives in `registerOpenApiEndpoints` and applies on both doors. The API route version (`api.version`) and the runtime version never enter `info.version`.
- ADR-0087 D3 entry for `api.documentation.version` (family `rest-api-documentation`); the liveness-ledger rows of the eight keys flip to enforced with the pin as evidence, the `version` row retires with the key.
- Pins: (1) all eight keys authored ⇒ the served `info` on both doors carries them and `info.version` is still `SPEC_VERSION`; (2) nothing authored, `documentation: {}`, and one key alone ⇒ `info` equals the artifact except the authored member — the #11646 pin (`rest-openapi-route.test.ts`) stays as the control; (3) an authored `documentation.version` is refused at parse with the tombstone message; (4) an authored `license` without `url` serves no `url`.
- Step one of #11646 (zero readers of the served `info.version` by value) was measured then and is not reopened.

State: `needs-user-decision` removed here; no `pm:*` state on this card — it is the ruling carrier, not the work card. #20294: `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`, its `Blocked-by: #20359` resolved by this comment (note there in the same stroke). The PR that lands #20294 closes this card too.
